To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The PE waveguide has the lowest bending loss among the waveguides we studied, and the optical power distribution in the LN layer is not sensitive to the PE thickness; (2) The strip-loaded waveguide has the highest bending loss, but the bending loss can be greatly reduced by increasing the thickness of the waveguide or by increasing the bending radius; (3) The ridge waveguide has an intermediate bending loss and is suitable for high-density integrated optical circuits.

we systematically studied the single-mode condition, the optical power distribution, the bending loss, and the dispersion of waveguides on lithium niobate thin films by a full-vector finite-difference method.

In summary, our research is concerned with
a systematical analysis of different kinds of waveguide structures on single crystal LiNbO3 thin film.
the analysis of the optical characteristics of waveguides on lithium niobate thin films.
the design of optical waveguide devices on LN thin films.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the waveguide structures are the most important factors that influence the optical power distribution, the bending loss and the coupling efficiency of the integrated optical devices.
the waveguide structures on lithium niobate thin films are suitable for the applications of high-density integrated optics.
PE and strip-loaded waveguides are more suitable for the realization of high-density integrated circuits than etched waveguides.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the strip-loaded waveguides are suitable for q-TE modes while PE and ridge waveguides are for q-TM modes.
the strip-loaded waveguides are suitable for the application of low bending loss, while the PE waveguides are more suitable for the application with high coupling efficiency.
the PE waveguide is suitable for the fabrication of high-performance optical components, and the strip-loaded and ridge waveguides are suitable for the fabrication on LN thin-film waveguide arrays.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the strip-loaded waveguides on thin films of lithium niobate are promising for the fabrication of high density integrated optical devices.
the strip-loaded waveguides have a low bending loss and the LN ridge waveguids are good for high-density integrated optical circuits.
ridge waveguides are a promising candidate for the realization of high-density integrated photonic circuits on thin film LiNbO3.
